text:
noah: FYI finished onboarding run for marlin-embed-wavelet on the multi-dataset recall bench. posting a condensed summary, want quick triage @meera @todd

meera: thanks. what are the headline deltas?

noah: float32 recall@10 = 0.691, L2-whitened float32 = 0.695. wavelet-compressed float32 (baseline transform) = 0.688. int8-perchannel after wavelet = 0.673. int6-perchannel = 0.682. latency: float32 14ms/embed, int8 8.9ms, int6 7.1ms.

todd: wavelet-compressed? explain quick — is that pre-processing on vectors before quant?

noah: yeah small orthogonal wavelet transform (Haar-based) applied to embeddings to reduce long-tail energy, then quantize. idea was to make quantization error more uniform across dims.

anya: interesting. how about clustering metrics? ARI / silhouette?

noah: ARI: float32 0.38, wavelet-float32 0.395, int6 0.36, int8 0.345. silhouette: float32 0.31, wavelet-float32 0.33, int6 0.29, int8 0.26. TSNEs and ARI table in artifacts.

meera: per-lang regressions? any weird langs?

noah: per-lang recall@10 deltas (int8-perchannel vs float32): en -0.009, fr -0.012, es -0.010, ru -0.020, ja -0.041. short queries (<7 tokens) worst hit: -0.034 abs on recall@10.

todd: ja again. do we know if tokenize length distribution differs a lot?

noah: looked at token len CDFs: japanese has many short-seq tokens (median 6) and higher variance in embedding norms. wavelet transform reduces norm skew a bit but int8 still clips tails.

meera: any fixes tried? small postnorm + per-channel scale tweak?

noah: experimented with three quick variants: (A) per-channel int8 + 10k calib, (B) per-channel int8 + stochastic rounding, (C) hybrid fp16 matmul + int8 KV cache. Results: A recall@10 0.676, B 0.679, C 0.685. C reduces ja gap to -0.022.

noah: eval snippet below for reproducibility:

```
# marlin quick-run
python eval_embeds.py \
  --model marlin-embed-wavelet \
  --preproc wavelet --wavelet haar \
  --quant MODE \
  --calib 10000 \
  --holdouts multi_recall_set.jsonl \
  --index hnsw --ef 160 --M 12 --dist l2 \
  --split short:lt7,long:gt128,langs:en,fr,es,ru,ja
```

noah: MODE = float32 | int8-perchannel | int6-perchannel | hybrid-fp16-int8. seeding: 4 seeds.

ci-bot: nightly-eval job marlin-2026-04-07 completed : artifacts -> s3://redwood-evals/marlin/6167778888/ (metrics.json, tsne_wavelet.png, norms_hist.png)

anya: did you try PQ on top of wavelet+int6? sometimes OPQ helps hide quant noise.

noah: OPQ+PQ(8) on int6 gave recall@10 0.678 (vs int6 raw 0.682) but index size -3.8x. interestingly OPQ with wavelet improved ARI by +0.02 vs no-OPQ.

meera: for product: what would you recommend for hosted vs dedicated?

noah: recommendation draft: Hosted: wavelet + float16 default (wavelet improves clustering and keeps variance low). Dedicated: offer int6-perchannel (wavelet preproc) as cost-saving opt-in; hybrid-fp16-int8 as intermediate canary. Block int8-perchannel as default until ja short-query regressions reduced < 1.5% abs.

meera: capture per-seed std and add small golden set for japanese short queries in the PR.

noah: will do. PR with full tables + minimal repro scripts forthcoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/980

todd: one more ask : include a simple ablation showing wavelet on/off for float32 and int6 so we can justify transform cost.

noah: good call, running ablation next. follow-ups listed in artifacts: (1) wavelet param sweep (haar vs db4), (2) calib-size sweep for int6 (1k/5k/10k), (3) hybrid latency microbench for KV cache.

eval-bot: label "wavelet-probe" added to PR #980 by noah

meera: thanks everyone, looks actionable. will review PR once CI completes.

noah: thanks all :rocket:
